dataset.name: Retail Demand Forecasting Dataset
dataset.source: Kaggle retail inventory and demand forecasting dataset
preprocessing_summary: Date values were parsed as datetime and checked for invalid records.
Duplicate rows were removed from the cleaned dataset.
Missing values were reviewed and no nulls remained in the final cleaned file.
The training pipeline keeps the temporal order of observations for split validation and test evaluation.

training.random_seed: Not recorded in the saved metadata
feature_engineering: Lag features for demand, inventory, units sold, units ordered, and price.
Rolling statistics over 7, 14, and 30 day windows for demand and inventory.
Calendar encodings with sine/cosine month and weekday transforms.
Inventory-demand ratio and inventory coverage approximations for operational context.
training.training_timestamp: Not recorded in the persisted training metadata

status.Demand Forecasting: Baseline endpoint only; trained model is not currently used for live forecast requests

findings: On the held-out test set, the XGBoost model achieved MAE 11.24 and RMSE 14.95, outperforming the mean baseline MAE 37.52 and RMSE 49.40.
The saved validation metrics also show XGBoost outperforming the baseline models on the same temporal holdout window.
The project does not contain saved residual distributions or feature-importance scores for the final deployed model artifact, so those charts are shown as not yet generated.
limitations: The dashboard forecast currently uses a seven-day moving-average baseline rather than the trained XGBoost model.
The project metadata does not include WAPE, a random seed, or final residual/error artifacts for the selected model.
The inventory optimization module is not backed by a validated lead-time and service-level policy, so stockout prevention claims should be treated as planned rather than implemented.
